rationale: ROUND 2. Round 1 returned REVISE on a gating objection from editquality, and it found a REAL defect that was live. The objection: pagePathFromContrastKey assumed a contrast_failure item_key is always 'contrast_failure:'+path+'#'+selector, and named the LANDMINE on this exact footprint - 'The render-audit package now holds TWO selector-composition schemes' - which I had not grepped. I measured both halves and both are live as of 2026-08-26. (a) A SELECTOR may itself contain '#': contrast_failure:/tools/sfi26-revenue-stacker/index.html#BUTTON#c-tool-... exists in production (1 of 469 open rows), and the describe scheme emits tag#id.classes by construction. (b) Far worse, a PAGE URL may contain '#': idea.uk carries BOTH /tools.html AND /tools.html#audience-check as ACTIVE pages, and has 35 open contrast_failure rows. So splitting on the first '#' turns a finding on the fragment page into one on /tools.html - a REAL page on that site - and the wrong page is prioritised, successfully and silently. Worth noting that the reviewer's own read-only check sampled 25 keys and every one conformed: the sample could not have found this, and the landmine did. THE FIX IS TO STOP PARSING. The priority matcher now works FORWARD from the live page set using the grader's own construction - workItemKey('contrast_failure', path+'#') then HasPrefix, which is literally write_render_audit_findings_action.go:748 - ordered longest-path-first so a shorter page cannot claim a longer one's rows. Ambiguity is unrepresentable rather than guarded against, and drift with the grader is impossible because both sides call the same composer. pagePathFromContrastKey is DELETED; a comment stands in its place recording the measurement so the next author does not re-add the inverse. Mutation-proven non-vacuously: reinstating the split fails the new test on idea.uk's real shape, restoring passes. EVERYTHING ELSE IS UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1 and is restated here because reviewers judge the plan against the rationale. bugs_open/394. request_render_audit selects a site's live pages ORDER BY COALESCE(nav_order,999), name and takes the first max_pages, so it takes the SAME deterministic prefix on every run. Pages past the cap are not audited less often - they have never been audited and never will be. bugs_closed/242 made this loud (a durable RENDER_AUDIT_TRUNCATED row) and raised the cap 25->60 as a stated mitigation; the signal has no reader and the mitigation has been outgrown. MEASURED 2026-08-26: webdesign.co.uk is 146 live pages, 60 audited, 86 never - and the tail is a CLASS, not a count. Its nav_order bands are 0..90 (6 nav pages), 100 (94 tools, alphabetical), 200 (48 tool-*-guide pages), 201 (1). The cap cuts between tool-head-architect and tool-html-minifier, so all 45 remaining guide pages are unreachable at ANY cap below 98, on a site that grew 15 pages in two days. That is why the bug's candidate 3 (raise the cap) is rejected on a measurement rather than a preference - and the premise is false anyway, because max_pages is per-DISPATCH not per-agent (the 2026-08-11 '5 of 26' row carries {"max_pages":5} under render-audit-agent, resolving the bug's own [UNEXPLAINED] note). So: a keyset coverage cursor, making max_pages a per-run spend dial instead of a coverage cliff. THE DECISION THIS TURNED ON: a plain cursor takes webdesign's per-page re-measurement latency to 3 days x ceil(146/60) = ~9 days. Migration 469 is an OWNER INSTRUCTION of 2026-08-18 whose stated why is that the render audit is the only thing that GRADES a contrast repair, so its window IS the confirmation latency of the repair loop, and seven days was unacceptable. A plain cursor therefore does not merely underperform that ruling, it exceeds the condition the owner ordered removed. It dissolves rather than trades: the protected population is not the site but the pages awaiting a grade, and MEASURED 2026-08-26 with the grader's own predicate that is 3 open contrast_failure items across 3 paths on webdesign (fleet max 17 paths, on a 37-page site that never truncates at 60). So the window is a UNION - the finding-bearing pages ride every run, the cursor covers the rest - at a cost of 3 of 60 slots. Grading latency stays at 469's 3 days; coverage of the 86 invisible pages goes from never to one cycle.

plan.summary: Give request_render_audit a keyset coverage cursor (opt-in, default off) whose window is the union of an open-contrast_failure priority set and the next N-k pages from the cursor, so the capped sweep rotates instead of repeating a prefix - while preserving the 3-day repair-grading latency migration 469 was commissioned to buy. Plus the reader the owner commissioned for RENDER_AUDIT_TRUNCATED, whose alarm conditions the cursor changes.

edits.rationale: The defect and its fix both live here. Adds one optional config key rotate_coverage (default false - the owner's 2026-08-02 rule that new authority on a shared seam ships opt-in with the unsafe side as the default; budget goes 6->7 of N=10). Selects the extra ordering columns, moves windowing into a pure helper, reads/writes the cursor, assembles the priority union, and splits the truncation message and context by mode. Prefix mode is byte-identical to today, which is what makes the two existing tests a compatibility guard rather than a rewrite.

Cursor arithmetic and priority selection as pure, testable functions. ROUND 2: the priority matcher no longer parses keys. pagesWithOpenContrastFindings builds one prefix per LIVE page with the shared composer and prefix-matches, longest path first, so a shorter page cannot claim a longer one's rows - idea.uk's /tools.html must not swallow /tools.html#audience-check. It returns the hit set, the total open row count, and the count of open rows matching NO live page (an item that can never self-grade, reported not acted on). The status predicate still interpolates sqlInList(workItemClosedStatuses), the grader's own constant.

ROUND 2 REVERSAL. Round 1 added pagePathFromContrastKey here; this edit REMOVES it and leaves a comment in its place. The inverse of the key composition is not safe to write: a selector may contain '#' (live: ...#BUTTON#c-tool-...) and a page URL may contain '#' (live: idea.uk has /tools.html and /tools.html#audience-check both active, with 35 open rows), so a first-'#' split silently attributes a finding to the wrong real page. The comment exists because the next author's instinct will be exactly mine was - the composer is right there, so write the inverse - and the measurement is what stops them.

Every guard proven by inducing the fault, never by observing zero findings. The two cases that matter most are the ones a natural test suite omits: a priority page must NOT advance the cursor (or the pages between it and the window are never audited by anything), and the priority context keys must be present when ZERO - a key that appears only on a bad run makes its absence ambiguous between none and binary-too-old.

The cursor table and the config flip must travel together - rotate_coverage true against a missing table would fail the first cursor read - so they are one transaction. _HOLD because the discovery runner hard-fails on a capability the binary lacks, so this must be applied by hand after the image rolls; the suffix matches run-migrations.sh's SIDECAR_RE so the runner lists it and skips it. The verify block is DO/RAISE, not SELECT: ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result, so a SELECT verify cannot stop the COMMIT.

Precedent 643. Rolling back must restore today's behaviour exactly, and it does so by construction: removing the key returns rotate to its default false, and dropping the table removes state the code only reads when rotate is true. The two must be undone in that order - key first, then table - or a run between the statements would read a missing table with rotate still on.

The reader the owner commissioned (decision 4, 2026-08-25). A cursor does not discharge it: it changes what the row MEANS, so the unhealthy variants need an alarm. Cloned from ungradedcompletions.go (DBG-077 shape). It must physically contain both RENDER_AUDIT_TRUNCATED and agent_error_log because the registry checker OPENS this file and greps it - a reader claim that cannot be satisfied by typing.

DBG-075 requires the flip in the SHIPPING commit, and the entry's own why says 'upgraded when it ships'. reader_sink is mandatory because consumed was silently ambiguous between a reader that reads the code and one that reads a different table - the field exists so an entry cannot pass the reader check while reading the wrong sink.

The render-audit package now holds TWO selector-composition schemes ... a landmine specifically about this exact key. If some existing rows use the other scheme, the p...'

Two schemes here is deliberate and permanent (council acadbe8b, reuse_agent seat).'

By scheme: 453 preserve-case (render-audit), 16 ancestor-anchored (leading '.'), 0 lowercase describe, and 1 row with MORE THAN ONE '#' — contrast_failure:/tools/sfi26-revenue-stacker/index.html#BUTTON#c-tool-sfi26-revenue-stacker-calculate-btn.

That site ALSO has /tools.html active, and 35 open contrast_failure rows. So a first-'#' split maps a finding on the fragment page onto a different REAL page on the same site.

Cap 60 cuts at rn 60 = tool-head-architect / rn 61 = tool-html-minifier, so all 45 remaining tool-*-guide pages at nav_order 200 are unreachable at any cap below 98.

sql_for_agents/469_render_audit_rotation_three_day_window.sql (OWNER INSTRUCTION 2026-08-18): 'The render audit is the only thing that GRADES a contrast repair: it re-measures the page in a browser and withdraws the work item if the defect has gone. Its eligibility window is therefore the confirmation latency of the whole repair loop: a fix that shipped today could wait up to SEVEN DAYS to be graded.'

And at :717-718: 'AllOfType is never set, and must not be: the wide branch would close every open contrast ticket for the site, including pages this run never opened.' So a rotating window cannot silently close findings on pages it skipped.

The priority query interpolates sqlInList(workItemClosedStatuses) rather than restating it.

sql_for_agents/346_site_discovery_rotation.sql: the table is 'Written by the site-discovery-rotation-* pre_queries; safe to TRUNCATE', last_selected_at is 'when the scheduler last PICKED the site', and stamping at selection is deliberate so 'a site whose run fails must not pin the rotation head and starve the fleet'. That is the precedent for advancing at dispatch, and the reason the cursor gets its own table rather than a column here.

MEASURED 2026-08-26 via scripts/audit-optional-key-budget.sh --json: request_render_audit declares 6 optional keys against the ruled budget of N=10 (WFA-013), and zero actions in the fleet are over budget. Adding rotate_coverage makes 7.

request_render_audit_action.go sets neither CheckConfig nor StrictConfig on RequestRenderAuditInputSpec (verified 2026-08-26), so an old binary meeting rotate_coverage in step config ignores it silently - every image/config skew order is inert rather than wrong.

LANDMINES, footprint CheckResult.Resolved: 'A monotonic check's if len(findings) == 0 { return } early return makes its new retraction INERT on exactly the sites that need it' - the reason the zero-priority context keys are asserted PRESENT rather than omitted, and the reason the truncation row is written before the produce while the cursor is written after.
plan.risks: ROUND 2 NOTE ON THE FIXED DEFECT: the parse is gone, so the class is closed rather than guarded — a wrong attribution is now unrepresentable, because the only thing compared is a prefix built by the shared composer from a page that is in this run's own live set. The residual is a matcher that is O(pages x rows); at today's fleet maximum that is 146 x 469 string comparisons on one site, once per audit dispatch, which is nothing beside tens of sequential Chromium navigations. REGRADE LATENCY IS PRESERVED; NEW-DEFECT DETECTION LATENCY IS PARTIALLY TRADED, and the second half must not be dropped when reporting the first. Preserved: every page carrying an open contrast_failure is in every run, so repair-grading and park-draining stay at the 3-day cadence migration 469 bought, bounded only by the half-window reserve (today 3 of a 30-slot reserve on the one truncating site). Traded: detection of a NEW defect on webdesign's first-60 pages degrades from every 3 days to one cycle (~9 days at 146 pages over a 57-slot rotation), because a page with no open finding has no claim on the priority set. In exchange, detection on the 86 structurally invisible pages goes from NEVER to one cycle. That is the actual bargain - head-page detection latency spent buying tail-page coverage, on exactly one site, at one cap. If ~9 days is unacceptable there, max_pages is now a pure latency dial with no coverage cliff behind it, so raising it for that one agent shortens the cycle without reintroducing the bug. SECOND: the priority set must not starve coverage. It is bounded at max_pages/2 so the rotation always keeps at least half the window, and the over-budget drop is selected cyclically from the cursor so the dropped excess is not the same pages every run - the deterministic-prefix disease reappearing in miniature, which is exactly what this change exists to remove. The drop is logged with the paths named and stamped durably in context; a silent cap here would be the original bug rebuilt one level down. THIRD: a stalled cursor is a new silent failure mode - if the cursor stops advancing, coverage looks healthy (rows keep arriving, mode says cursor) while nothing new is measured. That is precisely alarm condition (b) in the commissioned reader, and it is why the reader is in this submission rather than deferred. FOURTH: collation. The boundary is found by exact tuple match first and only falls back to Go tuple comparison, so Go-vs-Postgres ordering could differ only for a DELETED page with a non-ASCII name; page names are ASCII slugs today and the settling query is SELECT datcollate FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database(). FIFTH: the design-critique caller is left in prefix mode deliberately. It is manual-only with no cadence (its own seed file says so), its cap of 8 is plausibly meant as the most important 8 for a vision critique rather than any 8, and silently rotating what a critique looks at would change the product without anyone deciding to. It keeps writing prefix rows, which the reader acks by name - so a NEW unacked caller pages, and this one does not. SIXTH, stated because it is a real coupling rather than a hazard: what a clean result MEANS drifts over time. Cost per run is unchanged (same page count on the dedicated pod) but a clean cursor-mode result asserts cleanliness of its window, not of the site. findings_written already stamps truncated/pages_total/pages_audited from the echoed summary so no artefact claims whole-site, and the reader is the compensating control for the human habit of reading zero-inserted as site-clean.
